title: Assure and accelerate private inference deal playbook
body:
Goal: provide an executable, skimmable playbook teams can use to move regulated buyers from discovery -> pilot -> contract for private (VPC/on-prem) inference. Focus is on control plane language, realistic buyer objections, and concrete mitigations and asks.

High-level positioning (elevator, 30s):
- For regulated customers that need strong data stewardship and predictable inference economics, Redwood offers a private deployment path that keeps the control plane where customers require it (their VPC or on-prem environment) while still delivering our core runtime, rollout tooling, and observability. The result: enterprise-grade SLAs, clear auditability, and a path to scale without re-architecting your model stack.

One-pager value props to use with execs (CISO / CIO / CFO):
- CISO: Customer-managed control plane, full audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations, and explicit telemetry filters. We provide a minimal trust surface: Redwood only manages the orchestration layer you approve and never ingests customer payloads.
- CIO/CTO: Same API surface and rollout controls as our hosted offering; plug-and-play model upgrades, canary rollouts, and fallback policies while infrastructure and network live in your account.
- CFO: Predictable reserved capacity options, token-level cost breakdowns, and tooling to reduce unit costs (batching/caching/quantization) — with the ability to cap spend and choose commitment tiers.

Buyer personas & primary concerns (how to map objections):
- CISO: Data leakage, auditability, compliance scope, vendor access.
  - Typical objection: "How do I know Redwood can't read our data?"
  - Scripted response: "Your control plane lives in your VPC/accounts. Keys and telemetry are under your KMS. Redwood operators only have a control channel to deploy container images; they have no access to runtime plaintext. We supply signed attestation artifacts and an audit package for SOC2/ISO reviews."
- Procurement / Legal: Contractual SLAs, liability, termination.
  - Objection: "We need a contract with specific indemnities and data residency clauses."
  - Response: "We have a modular enterprise addendum covering indemnities, data processing terms, and export controls. For regulated pilots we often start with a limited-term pilot addendum to shorten procurement cycles."
- Platform/Infra: Network topology, observability, failover.
  - Objection: "Will this complicate our deployment topology and maintenance?"
  - Response: "We provide a streamlined deployment artifact (Helm/TF module or operator) and a runbook. Day-2 ops are minimized: automatic health checks, per-route telemetry, and standard SRE runbooks we co-author during onboarding."

Control plane language — recommended phrasing and commitments
- Use consistent phrases: "customer-managed control plane" (not "private control plane"), "no-plaintext-exfiltration guarantee", "customer KMS keys for secrets and model artifacts".
- Commitments to offer in pitch:
  - Control plane resources live in customer cloud account (or on-prem VM cluster).
  - Terraform/Helm templates are open and auditable prior to deployment.
  - Logs and telemetry retained per customer policy; Redwood only receives aggregated telemetry metrics unless explicit opt-in.
  - We can provide signed SBOMs and attestation for runtime images.

Pilot structure (recommended):
- Duration: 4–8 weeks.
- Minimum success criteria (SLA + acceptance tests):
  - Latency P50/P95 within agreed targets for a sampled workload.
  - Model-output fidelity smoke test (sample prompts + golden outputs) within acceptable deviation.
  - Audit package delivered: deployment manifests, SBOM, network diagram, and one week of full audit logs.
- Deliverables from Redwood: deployment artifact, runbook, performance tuning session, and a security onboarding checklist.
- Customer asks (to accelerate pilot): dedicated cloud account, KMS access to register keys, test dataset and prompt set for fidelity checks, and basic networking (peering/VPN) for initial traffic.

Negotiation levers and contracting tactics
- Short pilot addendum (time-boxed liability and limited data scope) to get past procurement.
- Tiered liability model: higher indemnity in exchange for higher ARR/commitment.
- Offer a capped proof-of-value month with credit offsets for early conversion.
- Break out professional services and onboarding fees to separate procurement lanes if needed.

Competitive callouts (talking points vs common alternatives)
- vs. managed cloud endpoints: managed endpoints simplify onboarding but typically keep control plane and telemetry in the vendor tenant — not acceptable for regulated data. Pitch: same developer ergonomics, but the control boundary is moved to the customer.
- vs. self-built inference stack: building is flexible but expensive and slow to iterate on performance and quantization. Pitch: Redwood provides production-grade runtime and optimization suggestions so teams get enterprise performance without rebuilding low-level runtime plumbing.

Technical mitigation checklist (what reviewers will ask for in security review)
- Deployment manifests (Terraform/Helm) for audit.
- SBOM + image signing and attestation.
- KMS integration and key rotation plan.
- Network diagram with least-privilege flows and egress controls.
- Access matrix: operators only allowed to deploy; no runtime key access.
- Pen test and internal vulnerability scan reports.

Quick objection-response crib sheet (snippets to drop into email / call):
- "Can Redwood see the data?" -> "No plaintext exfiltration — control plane in your account, keys in your KMS, logging as you specify."
- "We need to prove performance." -> "We run a short, instrumented perf pilot against a sample workload; P50/P95 baselines are produced within 2 weeks."
- "Procurement is slow." -> "We use a pilot addendum and separate professional services SOW to unblock initial work. Typical turnaround: 2–4 weeks with procurement support."

Sample email to CISO to start security review (short):
- Subject: Security onboarding for Redwood private inference pilot
- Body: Hi [Name], thanks for agreeing to evaluate Redwood. Attached: deployment manifests, SBOM, model handling controls, and a one-page network diagram. We propose a 4-week pilot with limited data and a completed audit package at week end. Can we schedule 45 minutes to walk the architecture next Tue/Thu?

Operational handoffs and internal GTM play steps
- AE to set expectation with buyer: need cloud account + test dataset + PO for pilot SOW.
- SE to run a 90-minute architecture alignment workshop (network, KMS, SSO).
- Security/Compliance SME to provide the audit package and answer questions during week 2.
- Solutions engineer to own performance tuning sessions and deliver final runbook.

Appendix — known blockers and mitigation patterns (real notes from early deals)
- Blocker: Buyer insists on private data plane and private control plane in their subnet.
  - Pattern: Offer a hybrid: control plane artifacts in customer account, runtime in their VPC with egress disabled; provide signed attestation and periodic audits.
- Blocker: Procurement demands unlimited liability.
  - Pattern: Offer a phased indemnity schedule tied to committed usage and an escrowed source build for on-prem installs in extreme cases.
- Blocker: Performance concerns at scale (low latency for interactive use).
  - Pattern: Prove via a 2-week perf run, present batching/kv-cache config changes, and offer reserved capacity pooling.

Next actions (for AE/SE):
- Templatize the pilot addendum and attach to every private-deploy play.
- Create a one-page architecture diagram template that maps to common cloud vendors (AWS/Azure/GCP) and a matching checklist.
- Ship security evidence packet: manifests + SBOM + attestation checklist + short pen test summary.

Notes to self / conversation fragments (informal):
- We should quantify typical time-to-value (pilot -> revenue) and call that out to CFOs. Early deals show conversion 8–14 weeks with active SE involvement.
- Need a simple public FAQ that explains difference between "control plane in customer account" vs "fully air-gapped on-prem" and the tradeoffs.

End of playbook. Use and adapt per account. This is intentionally pragmatic — the goal is to remove procurement friction and give SEs concrete lines to say to CISOs and procurement while preserving our ability to deliver a consistent runtime and observability experience.
